record.context_brief: embedded cmc surfaces with circular boundary
record.original_question: Is every compact embedded surface in R^3 with constant mean curvature and circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 (5*). Is a compact embedded cmc surface of R3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, connected, embedded smooth surface with boundary, having constant mean curvature, and whose boundary $\partial\Sigma$ is a round circle in some plane of $\mathbb{R}^3$. Must $\Sigma$ be either a flat planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap (a piece of a round sphere) bounded by that circle?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a long-standing open problem in the theory of constant mean curvature surfaces. Partial results are known under additional hypotheses (e.g., local convexity, stability, or symmetry of the surface), but the general embedded case remains unresolved as of recent literature. A 2024 preprint extending Liebmann's theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary establishes the result under a local convexity assumption, indicating the unrestricted problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: A locally convex, embedded, compact, connected CMC hypersurface bounded by a circle is a spherical cap.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture is approached under an extra local convexity assumption, indicating it is open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Whether spherical caps and flat disks are the only compact embedded CMC surfaces with circular boundary remains a central open question.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists the question as open.
